advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a non-IntentKind lifecycle override string falls back to the action-derived kind.
evidence: ticket_planner.py _intent_kind: 'override = m.payload.get("lifecycle"); if isinstance(override, str) and override in _INTENT_KIND_VALUES: return IntentKind(override)' then 'mapped = _ACTION_TO_KIND.get(m.action.value)'
advisory.finding: The _intent_kind invalid-override fallback is untested: an explicit payload['lifecycle'] that is a string but not one of the six IntentKind values must fall through to the action mapping (override ignored), but only a VALID 'rekey' override is exercised. A named violating input: a mutation with action='create' and payload={'lifecycle':'notakind'} should still derive kind 'bind', not raise or produce None.
scenarios: A mutation carries a mistyped/unknown lifecycle override string

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_mode_capped` distinguish write-enabled modes (bootstrap-strict/throttle/live) from read-only modes (reconcile-check/dry-run) instead of treating every non-'live' mode as capping all outbound work.
evidence: ticket_planner.py:99-101: `def _mode_capped(muts, mode): return mode != "live" and any(m.direction.value == "outbound" for m in muts)`
mode.py:41-45 defines RECONCILE_CHECK='reconcile-check', DRY_RUN='dry-run', BOOTSTRAP_STRICT='bootstrap-strict', BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE='bootstrap-throttle', LIVE='live'
mode.py:36-37 documents BOOTSTRAP_STRICT/THROTTLE as modes that DO write ('writes only on high-confidence deltas' / 'writes on most deltas with rate-limiting')
Test asserts the coarse gate: test_ticket_plan_shadow.py uses `mode="check"` (not even a real Mode value) and expects outbound → safety_aborted, confirming the check is a literal '!= live' comparison
blocking.finding: `_mode_capped` treats every mode string other than the literal 'live' as capping all outbound mutations to `safety_aborted`, but the `Mode` enum defines `bootstrap-strict` and `bootstrap-throttle` as write-enabled modes ('writes only on high-confidence deltas' / 'writes on most deltas'). Under either bootstrap mode the shadow planner defers every outbound-bearing plan as safety_aborted, which contradicts those modes' documented write behavior.
scenarios: A reconcile pass driven at Mode.BOOTSTRAP_STRICT or BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE: every outbound-bearing ticket plan is deferred safety_aborted in the shadow layer even though the mode permits writes.
blocking.suggested_fix: Cap only for read-only modes, e.g. `mode not in {"live", "bootstrap-strict", "bootstrap-throttle"}` (or reuse Mode.rank/ordering), rather than `mode != "live"`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether a `lifecycle` payload override may promote a probe/conflict action to a lifecycle intent, and gate the override to mapping-eligible actions if not intended.
evidence: ticket_planner.py:171-175: override wins unconditionally: `override = m.payload.get("lifecycle"); if isinstance(override, str) and override in _INTENT_KIND_VALUES: return IntentKind(override)`
ticket_planner.py:60 comment: `# Default action → lifecycle intent kind mapping (probe/conflict map to no kind).`
test_probe_and_conflict_actions_yield_no_intent only covers probe/conflict WITHOUT a lifecycle override, so the override-on-probe path is unspecified
dropped.finding: `_intent_kind` applies an explicit `payload['lifecycle']` override even for actions that otherwise derive no intent kind (probe/conflict), so a probe/conflict mutation carrying `lifecycle` synthesizes a lifecycle intent, while the docstring/`_ACTION_TO_KIND` comment states probe/conflict map to no kind.
scenarios: A probe or conflict mutation whose payload carries `lifecycle: "bind"` produces a bind LifecycleIntent, contradicting the 'probe/conflict → no kind' contract.

evidence: ticket_plan.py __eq__: 'return (self.kind == other.kind and self.target == other.target and self.version == other.version and self.payload == other.payload)'

dropped.finding: The new LifecycleIntent type's equality (__eq__ compares payload) and hash (__hash__ excludes payload) contract is untested: no test constructs two LifecycleIntent values to assert that two intents with identical kind/target/version but differing payload are unequal yet hash-equal (the documented identity/hash split). A regression that dropped payload from __eq__ or added it to __hash__ would not be caught.
merged_from: LifecycleIntent.__post_init__ deep-freezes its payload, but no test asserts the derived intent's payload is frozen/immutable. Intent payload is never read in any assertion (only kind/version are), so a regression removing the _deep_freeze call on intents would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor changes which fields participate in LifecycleIntent equality/hash
Two intents differing only in payload are wrongly treated as equal
